cards.front: Define scalar multiplication of a matrix $A$ by a scalar $k$.
cards.back: Scalar multiplication is an operation that multiplies every element (entry) of a matrix $A$ by a single number (scalar) $k$. The result is a new matrix of the same dimensions as $A$.

cards.front: Given a matrix $A = [a_{ij}]$ and a scalar $k$, express the resulting matrix $kA$ using element notation.
cards.back: If $A = [a_{ij}]$, then $kA = [k \cdot a_{ij}]$. This means each element $a_{ij}$ in matrix $A$ is multiplied by the scalar $k$ to form the corresponding element in the new matrix $kA$.

cards.front: State the property of scalar multiplication that relates it to matrix addition for scalars $k$ and matrices $A, B$ of the same dimensions.
cards.back: Scalar multiplication is distributive over matrix addition: $k(A+B) = kA + kB$.

cards.front: State the property of scalar multiplication that relates it to scalar addition for scalars $k, m$ and a matrix $A$.
cards.back: Scalar multiplication is distributive over scalar addition: $(k+m)A = kA + mA$.

cards.front: State the associative property involving two scalars $k, m$ and a matrix $A$ for scalar multiplication.
Simplify the expression $2(3A - B) + 4B$, where $A$ and $B$ are matrices of compatible dimensions.
What is the result of multiplying any matrix $A$ by the scalar $0$?
cards.back: Multiplying any matrix $A$ by the scalar $0$ results in a zero matrix of the same dimensions as $A$. That is, $0 \cdot A = \mathbf{0}$, where $\mathbf{0}$ is the zero matrix (all elements are zero).

cards.front: What is the result of multiplying any matrix $A$ by the scalar $1$?
cards.back: Multiplying any matrix $A$ by the scalar $1$ results in the original matrix $A$. That is, $1 \cdot A = A$.
